label: SIMULATION
title: Experiment 6: Planner efficiency (SIMULATION)
headline: In simulation (200 random two-variable boundaries), choosing each test by uncertainty found the minimum extinction oxygen within 0.5 points in a median of 11 tests (80th percentile 14) versus 24 (80th percentile 30) for the plan's fixed 6x6 test matrix, with 100% vs 86% success.
claim: Choosing each test by uncertainty needed about half the tests of a fixed matrix run in the plan's order, in simulation (median 11 vs 24 tests, success 100% vs 86%, 200 simulated two-variable boundaries); a matrix that includes 1.1 atm, where the simulated minimum always lies, and runs that row first needed fewer at the median (9) but succeeded less often (92%) and had a longer tail (80th percentile 23.4 vs 14).
caveats: The saving depends on how the fixed matrix is laid out. MOC rises as pressure falls, so the simulated minimum always lies at 1.1 atm. A 6x6 matrix that includes 1.1 atm and runs that row first needed a median of 9 tests (80th percentile 23.4, success 92%). The uncertainty-driven planner, given no hint about where the hazard lies, needed a median of 11 (80th percentile 14, success 100%). The planner's advantage is that it does not need that prior knowledge, not that it beats every matrix at the median. See the fixed-matrix layout table.
